ops.title: Design item: lenient print-parse mode for malformed -p stream sections
ops.body:
Surfaced by the cc-context/bench v14 migration (P8): bench's `trajectory.py` kept one raw scrape because `parse_print_result` is strict — a malformed or truncated section in a `-p` (print-mode) stream fails the whole parse, so consumers that only need the well-formed tail (e.g. the final result message with `PrintMessage.id`/`usage`) can't use the typed layer on imperfect captures. The stewardship pushback during the fix round upgraded "leave consistency_section raw" from a silent accept to this tracked design item.

Proposed shape (design, not committed): a lenient mode on the print-parse entry point that yields typed messages for parseable elements and a typed `MalformedSection` marker (raw bytes + offset) for the rest, instead of raising. Strict stays the default — lenient is opt-in for salvage/analytics consumers like bench. Owner module: the print-result parsing layer in cc-transcript core (Rust) with the Python view on top; per AGENTS.md § Ownership, no consumer-side regex fallbacks in the meantime.
